sections.overview: The Silver-eared Mesia is a small babbler of the Himalayan foothills and Southeast Asian hills.
sections.identification: Its black cap and silver ear patches distinguish it from the related Red-billed Leiothrix, Leiothrix lutea.
sections.habitat: It uses evergreen forest, scrub and secondary growth in hills and mountains.
sections.diet: It eats insects, berries and seeds, foraging among foliage.
sections.behavior: It often forages actively in noisy groups in the forest understorey.
sections.reproduction: It builds a cup-shaped nest in a low shrub, usually laying about four eggs.
sections.ecology: The Red-billed Leiothrix is its closest familiar relative; their head markings distinguish the two.
sections.conservation: Oiseaux.net reports it as Least Concern on the IUCN Red List.
